question: What is the upper portion of the earth's mantle called?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Asthenosphere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The asthenosphere is the ductile part of the earth's upper mantle, situated directly below the lithosphere.
 
• It plays a crucial role in tectonic plate movements as it allows the lithosphere to move on top of it.
 
• The asthenosphere is composed of partially molten rock, which makes it mechanically weak and easily deformable.
 
• It extends from about 100 km to 200 km below the earth's surface.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lithosphere**

 
 
• The lithosphere is the rigid, outermost shell of a terrestrial planet, including Earth.
 
• It consists of the crust and the uppermost part of the mantle, which is rigid.
 
• The lithosphere is divided into tectonic plates that move and interact at their boundaries, causing earthquakes, volcanic activity, and mountain building.
 
• It is typically about 100 km thick.
 
 
 
• **Troposphere**
 
 
• The troposphere is the lowest layer of Earth's atmosphere and where all weather occurs.
 
• It extends up to 8-15 km above sea level, depending on the latitude and season.
 
• Temperature decreases with height in the troposphere.
 
• It contains approximately 75% of the atmosphere's mass and 99% of its water vapor and aerosols.
 
 
 
• **Stratosphere**
 
 
• The stratosphere is the second layer of Earth's atmosphere, lying above the troposphere and below the mesosphere.
 
• It extends from about 15 km to 50 km above the Earth's surface.
 
• Temperature increases with height in the stratosphere due to the absorption of ultraviolet radiation by the ozone layer.
 
• Commercial jets often fly in the lower stratosphere to avoid turbulence in the troposphere.
